content.text:
The file was introduced in this single commit (b463960) which added `CustomPieChart.java` for the first time, and that initial version already contained the malformed code — the anonymous inner class body directly contained an `if` statement without being wrapped in the `performHighlight` method override, with unused imports (`View`, `ChartTouchListener`, `OnChartGestureListener`) left in. This is not valid Java and wouldn't compile as intended (or silently fails to override the highlight behavior since the method signature is missing). The fix commit simply corrects this by adding the missing `protected void performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e) {` method declaration and removing the unused imports.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b4639602a22a16c7bd671ffd1cc2d1dafabd501d

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the file history of `CustomPieChart.java` (the only file touched by the bug-fix commit) using `git log --follow`, which showed only two commits ever touched this file: `b463960` (creation) and `dc4ddf0` (the fix itself).

(2) I inspected `b463960`'s diff and found it added `CustomPieChart.java` from scratch, and the added code already contained the exact same structural defect that `dc4ddf0` fixes: the `if (h != null && !h.equalTo(mLastHighlighted)) {...}` block sits directly inside the anonymous `PieRadarChartTouchListener` subclass body, not inside any method — meaning the intended override of `performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e)` was never actually declared. This is invalid/non-functional Java (the highlight-suppression behavior the class's own doc comment claims to provide — "Override to disable unhighlight function" — was never actually wired up). The unused imports (`View`, `ChartTouchListener`, `OnChartGestureListener`) that the fix removes were also already present in this same commit, confirming it's the same code block, untouched, being repaired.

(3) Since no other commit modified this file between `b463960` and `dc4ddf0`, and the defective code is verbatim present at creation time, `b463960` is the commit that introduced the bug. There is no ambiguity here — this is a single-commit, single-file bug introduction with high confidence.
